name: veterinary_clinic_system_053_problem_list_rollup
instruction: Build the practice's active-problem census under this episode's batch code (read batch_code from the ops_meta row with meta_key='episode_state'). A problem counts only when its entry inside a visit_records row's problems array has status='active' — resolved or other statuses, and rows with an empty problems array, contribute nothing. Write two report sets into ops_reports, first deleting any existing rows with report in ('problem_census','problem_census_by_location') and batch_code=<batch_code>: (1) report='problem_census' — exactly one row per problem name that has at least one active occurrence anywhere, each {report:'problem_census', batch_code, problem:<name>, active_cases:<count of active occurrences across all visit rows>, distinct_patients:<count of distinct patient_ids carrying an active entry of this name>, distinct_locations:<count of distinct visit_records.location_id values where it occurs>, distinct_species:<count of distinct patients.species values among those patients>}. (2) report='problem_census_by_location' — exactly one row per (problem name, location_id) pair that has at least one active occurrence at that location, each {report:'problem_census_by_location', batch_code, problem:<name>, location_id:<that visit_records location_id>, active_cases:<count>, distinct_patients:<count of distinct patient_ids>}. No rows for zero-count names or pairs, and no other rows or collections may be touched — the census is a read of visit_records and patients only.
_par_steps_note: Intentionally unset — measure real gold API-call count via a live gold run in the QC session (codegen-only pass).
_max_steps_note: Intentionally unset — set to roughly par_steps * 1.5 in the QC session per the anti-brute-force rule.

success_criteria.summary: Verifier recomputes the census from live (canary-pinned) visit_records + patients two independent ways — a raw-row Python pass over the problems arrays and an independent SQL json_array_elements/GROUP BY — and both must agree with each other and with the written ops_reports rows: exactly len(active problem names) 'problem_census' rows and len(active problem×location pairs) 'problem_census_by_location' rows for this batch_code, every field exact. All 23 other seeded collections are canary-hashed unchanged.

checks.expect: every active_cases / distinct_* number agrees between raw-row Python aggregation and an independent SQL json_array_elements + GROUP BY query

hazards: Rows-vs-patients trap: patient 59 carries 'atopic dermatitis' with status='active' on two different visit rows (ids 118 and 331) — the census must report active_cases=15 but distinct_patients=14 for that name; counting rows for distinct_patients (or patients for active_cases) flips exactly one field and fails.

Status filter: resolved entries exist under the same problem names (e.g., visit id=1 has 'chronic kidney disease' status='resolved'; visit id=20 has 'atopic dermatitis' status='resolved'; visit id=19 'obesity' resolved) — filtering on name alone inflates every aggregate.
Sparse-array trap: 208 of the 371 visit rows carry an empty problems array — a solution that assumes every row has problems either crashes or fabricates phantom cases.

distinct_species requires the patients join: problem names span different species mixes (chronic kidney disease spans 5 species, hypothyroidism 3, obesity 4) — a solution that copies distinct_patients into distinct_species or guesses the species count fails field-level checks.

The (problem, location) grid must be derived, not fabricated: in this seed all 7 problem names appear at all 3 locations (21 rows), but each cell's counts differ — e.g., atopic dermatitis is 7 cases / 6 patients at location 1 but 1 case / 1 patient at location 3; uniform or cross-product guesses fail.
Idempotency: the report set is deleted-then-rewritten keyed by (report, batch_code); a naive re-run double-pushes duplicate rows and fails the exact row-count checks.

uniqueness_searches.query: RL benchmark task nested JSON problem array census distinct patients locations species two-level rollup
top_results: No public benchmark task found combining nested problem-array aggregation with distinct-patient and per-location dimensions
Existing medical-record aggregation tasks are flat row counts, not array-element unnesting
Veterinary problem-list documentation describes the concept but not a verifiable multi-dimensional census

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Upgrades v1's single-level problem census into a two-level rollup: per-problem totals now carry three distinct-count dimensions (patients, locations, species — the last requiring a patients join) plus a full problem×location breakdown. The seed's rows-vs-patients asymmetry (one patient with two active entries of the same problem) and the 208 empty problems arrays make naive aggregation wrong in non-obvious ways.
